integrity.composition_basis: For opposite matrix units, XY is nonzero exactly when the target index of Y equals the source index of X, and YX is nonzero exactly when the target index of X equals the source index of Y.
integrity.euler_basis: Euler characteristic localizes to the fixed locus for algebraic C* actions on complex projective varieties.
integrity.first_public_date_basis: The bibliographic record for the Inventiones paper gives publication date 1999-09-29.
integrity.fixed_point_basis: A generic diagonal cocharacter has matrix-unit coordinate points as the only fixed points in each projective matrix factor.
integrity.object_basis: The archival literature defines the two-step circular-complex variety by XY=0 and YX=0 and identifies its irreducible components by dense-orbit rank pairs.
integrity.primary_slot_basis: The zbMATH-linked classification record lists MSC 14M05 first for the archival circular-complex paper; all listed classifications are algebraic-geometry codes.
integrity.rank_independence_basis: Every surviving fixed coordinate pair has rank one in both matrix factors, so it lies in every nontrivial rank closure.

scientific_limitations: The theorem computes ordinary Euler characteristic only; component dimensions, Betti numbers, Hodge numbers, singularities, and multidegrees can differ.
The biprojective model requires both arrows to be nonzero and therefore excludes the affine coordinate axes.
The localization proof is short, so an older unindexed or folklore computation remains possible.
title: Rank-independent Euler characteristic of biprojective circular-complex components
